$comment: Not a schema: the frozen v1 baseline of the Gateway contract (#1314). Every served operation, the components it reaches, its security schemes, the served limits and the problem registry as published. scripts/check_gateway_contract.py fails when the current contract breaks one of them; --freeze only appends entries, and CI rejects any other edit.

get.description: Read the authenticated Principal's own session (#302, ADR-134 §5): its entities, the effective grants the host derives from its recorded authority, its consent, the current execution mode with the operator network grants and the Principal's network posture, and the EPF1 execution profile. Nothing is echoed from the request: the acting entity only selects the decision. The read is protected like every other operation: the Local Principal's grant must cover `session.read` for the acting entity.

post.description: Revoke one of the acting Principal's own consents (#309, ADR-039), named by the `EventId` of its `consent.granted.v1` Event (`consent_ref`, D7), as the Principal's `Session` lists it. The revocation is one `consent.revoked.v1` Event on the Principal's consent Timeline; its sequence is the ADR-039 fence. It is recorded after every protected operation admitted before it completes and takes effect before the next decision: from then on every operation the consent governs is `403 revoked`, while the operations no consent governs (among them reading the Session and revoking a consent) stay available. Revocation stops future protected work; it is distinct from erasure and deletes nothing. It is monotonic: revoking a revoked consent returns its original revocation (`200`). The operation itself requires the `consent.revoke` grant like any protected operation.

ActionRequest.description: One typed simulated action. It affects simulation state only; no route creates a real-world effect.

EventCursor.description: An opaque continuation cursor bound to one Timeline and one host inventory generation. Clients pass it back unchanged; a cursor of an older generation is `append-conflict`.

EventPage.description: One page of committed Events in ascending Timeline Order. `next_from_seq` is null only when the Timeline is exhausted; `next_cursor` is null when the host binds no inventory generation.

EventView.description: A committed Event. `seq` is its position in Timeline Order and is the commit receipt; `event_type` names its schema.

payload.description: The decoded payload when the canonical CBOR is JSON-compatible; absent otherwise.

OwnTracksLocation.description: An OwnTracks `location` message; every other member is discarded by minimization.

Problem.description: An RFC 9457 problem details body. `code` is the stable family of problem-types.json; `type` is its URN. `detail` is safe human-readable text whose wording is not part of the contract.

instance.description: The matched route template of the failed request; the request path only for an unrouted request.

retryable.description: Whether an identical retry may succeed later.

IdempotencyKey.description: A caller-generated key of 1 to 128 visible ASCII characters. Repeating the key with the same request bytes returns the original result; reusing it with different bytes is `idempotency-conflict`.

WorldActionV1.description: The typed `world.action.v1` proposal. `params` are two JSON floats (X, Z, metres per second); integers are rejected at admission as `admission-rejected` (JSON Schema cannot distinguish them).

Session.description: The authenticated Principal's own session: its entities, effective grants, consent, the current execution mode (`mode_profile`, with the operator network grants and this Principal's network posture) and the EPF1 execution profile. `id` is the Principal's ID. `generation` is the authority generation: the head position of the Principal's recorded authority chain plus the head of its consent Timeline (0 when its grant binds none), so it advances on every grant, consent or revocation change and never uses wall time. `provenance.digest` is BLAKE3(UTF-8 `PiglorOS.GatewaySession.v1` || 0x00 || the 16 bytes of the 128-bit big-endian value of `id` decoded as a Crockford base32 ULID || `generation` as a big-endian u64 || the ASCII `mode_profile.mode_profile_digest` || `mode_profile.binding_epoch` as a big-endian u64), and its origin is `host-derived`. The digest covers the Principal, the generation, the mode digest and the epoch only: the entities, grants and network grants move with the authority head and the binding epoch. `contract.contract_version` is `1.0.0-draft` until Wave 9 acceptance and `1.0.0` from then on; a client accepts both.

grants.description: The names of the operations and capabilities the Principal's recorded grant covers for the acting entity, sorted, as the host's own authority evaluator decides them; a client never supplies a trusted capability. The DomainKey `gateway.network.v1` is the Principal network capability (ADR-134 §4): it authorizes no operation in v1 and only decides the `mode_profile.network` disclosure; it is granted only through explicit-grant provisioning, never an operator flag. A listed name means the grant covers that capability, not that the operation will succeed: the operation may still be refused for its own reasons.

consent_ref.description: The EventId (ULID) of the consent's `consent.granted.v1` Event (D7).

contract_version.description: The contract version the Gateway serves: `1.0.0-draft` until Wave 9 acceptance, then `1.0.0`.

DomainKey.description: A canonical lower-case ASCII identifier (so its length in characters is its length in bytes): a capability, dimension, Plugin, rule or option key.

ResourceEnvelope.description: The members every enveloped resource (Session and each Draft resource) carries: its schema identifier, resource ID, exactly one of an immutable `revision` or a monotonic `generation`, a provenance reference, the GMP1 `mode_profile` it was produced under (Session: the current binding), the EPF1-only `execution_profile` and capability-filtered availability. Ordering uses Timeline sequence, Fork generation and schema ordinals, never wall time. Each resource schema composes this envelope and closes itself with `unevaluatedProperties`. Server invariant: an `installed` `execution_profile.profile_id` is in the servable set of `mode_profile.mode` (README rule 3).

revision.description: An immutable revision; a change is a new revision.

generation.description: A monotonic generation; it never decreases.

mode_profile.description: Session reports `session-mode-profile` (the current binding); every other resource reports `mode-profile` (the binding it was produced under).

Availability.description: Capability-filtered availability. Each withheld member names why it is absent, so unknown, unauthorized, revoked, deleted and unavailable stay distinct; an `available` resource withholds nothing.

ExecutionProfile.description: The ADR-104 EPF1 execution profile a resource was produced under, or its explicit absence. It never carries the serving mode, which is `mode_profile`. Until #461 installs an EPF1 every Gateway resource reports `state: unavailable` with `reason: not-installed`. When `installed`, `profile_id` is the ADR-058 family and `profile_digest` the raw EPF1 digest; `profile_id` is always in the servable set of the resource's mode (a server invariant, README rule 3).

state.description: `installed` or `unavailable`. The set is deliberately closed in v1.

reason.description: Why no EPF1 is reported. Open within v1; server invariant: `not-installed` is the only reason the Gateway emits.

ModeProfile.description: The GMP1 a resource was produced under (ADR-134 §5). A resource materialized from committed Events or stored revisions reports the binding epoch recorded in its producing commit's evidence; a resource computed per request reports the epoch current when it is computed. The history record of an epoch never changes, so the disclosure stays stable across later rotation or migration. Only Session reports the current mode.

ProvenanceReference.description: The digest of the resource's provenance record and its origin class. Provenance describes lineage only; it is not a signature, conformance or calibration claim.

origin.description: The origin class of the provenance record. The set is deliberately closed in v1.

SessionModeProfile.description: The current GMP1 binding of the serving store, with the operator's network grants and this Principal's network posture (ADR-134 §5). `network` is `absent` in Air-Gapped mode; in Local mode it is `capability-granted` only when the GMP1 allows network and the Principal holds the capability `gateway.network.v1`, otherwise `denied`. `gateway.network.v1` authorizes no operation in v1. Clients should show `network_grants` next to `network`, so an operator-exposed spectator or OwnTracks ingress stays visible when the Principal's own network is `denied`.

network_grants.description: The operator's `--network-grant` values, sorted. Open within v1; server invariant: only `owntracks` and `public-read-only` exist, and Air-Gapped accepts none.

network.description: The Principal's network posture: `absent`, `denied` or `capability-granted`. The set is deliberately closed in v1.

Digest.description: A BLAKE3-256 digest in lower-case hex.

ExecutionProfileId.description: An ADR-058 execution profile family: a versioned lower-case slug, never in the `gateway-mode-` namespace of `GatewayModeProfileId`. The set is open so a later family (such as the live Air-Gapped family of #1372) stays within v1; a client handles an identifier it does not know as an unknown profile. Server invariant in v1: the Gateway names only `replay-v1`, `deterministic-local-v1`, `deterministic-air-gapped-v1` and `live-local-v1`, and a Local deployment never reports an Air-Gapped profile (the servable sets of README rule 3).

ModeProfileIdentity.description: The members that identify one GMP1 binding: its kind, profile, mode, digest and store binding epoch. `mode_profile_digest` is BLAKE3(UTF-8 `PiglorOS.GatewayModeProfile.v1` || 0x00 || canonical GMP1 bytes), recomputable from `execution-mode-profiles.json`. `mode` pairs with `mode_profile_id`. The schemas that compose it close themselves.

mode.description: The serving mode the profile declares. Open within v1; server invariant: `local` for `gateway-mode-local-v1` and `air-gapped` for `gateway-mode-air-gapped-v1` (the pairing below), and no other mode.

binding_epoch.description: The store binding epoch: 1 at bind, incremented on every rotation and migration (ADR-134 §8).

GatewayModeProfileId.description: A Gateway execution-mode profile (GMP1, ADR-134 §1). Its `gateway-mode-` namespace is disjoint from the ADR-058 `ExecutionProfileId`: neither is ever accepted where the other is expected. The profiles are composition-verified, never installed, qualified or a reproducibility claim; their public declaration is `execution-mode-profiles.json`. The set is open, so an ADR-134 amendment may add a profile within v1. Server invariant in v1: the Gateway serves only `gateway-mode-local-v1` and `gateway-mode-air-gapped-v1`.

ConsentRevocation.description: A recorded consent revocation (#309). `id` is the `EventId` of its `consent.revoked.v1` Event and `generation` the revocation's ADR-039 fence: its sequence on the Principal's consent Timeline, from which it is effective. It is the consent fence, not the `Session` authority generation (D8): a `Session` read at or after the revocation reports `generation` greater than or equal to it. It stops future protected work the consent governs and is distinct from erasure. `provenance.digest` is BLAKE3(UTF-8 `PiglorOS.GatewayConsentRevocation.v1` || 0x00 || the 16 bytes of the 128-bit big-endian value of the Principal's ID (its `Session` `id`) decoded as a Crockford base32 ULID || `generation` as a big-endian u64 || the ASCII `mode_profile.mode_profile_digest` || `mode_profile.binding_epoch` as a big-endian u64), and its origin is `host-derived`. `mode_profile` is the binding the revocation's commit was produced under, so every answer about one revocation is the same.

schema_version.description: The schema version of the request; any other version is `400 unsupported-version`.

tags.description: A set of keys; the revision answers them in byte order.

x_micro.description: A value in integer micro-units (10^-6) for deterministic Replay.

z_micro.description: A value in integer micro-units (10^-6) for deterministic Replay.

options.description: The user-supplied alternatives, in the order the revision keeps; a key appears once (checked at admission). A label is at most 128 UTF-8 bytes (`x-pigloros-limits.label_bytes`).

CreateOptionSpecRequest.description: Without `parent` it creates revision 1 of a new OptionSpec; with `parent` the next revision, whose current head `parent` must name (`409 append-conflict` otherwise). The subject is the acting entity, as for a Preference. Identical content is never deduplicated.

CreatePreferenceRequest.description: Without `parent` it creates revision 1 of a new Preference; with `parent` it creates the next revision of that Preference, whose current head `parent` must name (`409 append-conflict` otherwise). The subject is the acting entity (`x-piglor-actor-entity`), which the Local Principal's grant must cover; a parent of another subject is `404 not-found-or-unavailable`. Identical content is never deduplicated: a retry is recognized only by its `Idempotency-Key`.

schema_version.description: The schema version of the request; any other version is `400 unsupported-version`.

weights.description: Named dimension weights in [-1, 1] as integer micro-units; a dimension appears once (checked at admission). They are a set: the revision answers them ordered by `dimension`.

OptionSpecRevision.description: One immutable subject-scoped OptionSpec revision, answered only to its subject: any other caller gets the same `404 not-found-or-unavailable` as for an unknown revision. A revision its subject erased answers `410 deleted` to that subject from a payload-free tombstone and `404 not-found-or-unavailable` to everyone else; no erased value is reconstructed. `provenance.origin` is `principal-authored`, and `mode_profile` is the binding the producing commit recorded. `provenance.digest` is BLAKE3 of `PiglorOS.GatewayRevisionProvenance.v1`, a 0x00 byte and the deterministic CBOR array `[origin, principal_id, subject_entity_id, mode_profile_id, mode_profile_digest, binding_epoch, digest]` (text, ULIDs and lower-case hex digests, `binding_epoch` an unsigned integer): the authoring Principal (`Session.principal.principal_id`) and the execution-mode binding the producing commit recorded.

schema_version.description: The schema version the revision was created under.

subject_entity_id.description: The subject the revision is scoped to: the acting entity that created it.

x_micro.description: A value in integer micro-units (10^-6) for deterministic Replay.

z_micro.description: A value in integer micro-units (10^-6) for deterministic Replay.

options.description: The user-supplied alternatives in their authored order, each with its tags in byte order.

digest.description: BLAKE3 of the ASCII domain tag `PiglorOS.GatewayOptionSpecRevision.v1` followed by a 0x00 byte and the revision's canonical bytes: the RFC 8949 §4.2.1 deterministic CBOR array `[schema_id, schema_version, id, revision, parent_revision, subject_entity_id, options]` (IDs as canonical ULID text, `parent_revision` null for revision 1), where each option is `[key, label, tags, lean_hint_micro, coordinates]` in revision order, with `tags` in byte order, `lean_hint_micro` null when absent and `coordinates` the array `[x_micro, z_micro]` or null. A `revision-ref` names a revision by its `id`, `revision` and this digest.

PreferenceRevision.description: One immutable subject-scoped Preference revision, answered only to its subject: any other caller gets the same `404 not-found-or-unavailable` as for an unknown revision. A revision its subject erased answers `410 deleted` to that subject from a payload-free tombstone and `404 not-found-or-unavailable` to everyone else; no erased value is reconstructed. `provenance.origin` is `principal-authored`, and `mode_profile` is the binding the producing commit recorded. `provenance.digest` is BLAKE3 of `PiglorOS.GatewayRevisionProvenance.v1`, a 0x00 byte and the deterministic CBOR array `[origin, principal_id, subject_entity_id, mode_profile_id, mode_profile_digest, binding_epoch, digest]` (text, ULIDs and lower-case hex digests, `binding_epoch` an unsigned integer): the authoring Principal (`Session.principal.principal_id`) and the execution-mode binding the producing commit recorded.

schema_version.description: The schema version the revision was created under.

subject_entity_id.description: The subject the revision is scoped to: the acting entity that created it.

weights.description: Named dimension weights in [-1, 1] as integer micro-units, ordered by `dimension`.

digest.description: BLAKE3 of the ASCII domain tag `PiglorOS.GatewayPreferenceRevision.v1` followed by a 0x00 byte and the revision's canonical bytes: the RFC 8949 §4.2.1 deterministic CBOR array `[schema_id, schema_version, id, revision, parent_revision, subject_entity_id, weights]` (IDs as canonical ULID text, `parent_revision` null for revision 1), where each weight is `[dimension, weight_micro]`, ordered by `dimension`. A `revision-ref` names a revision by its `id`, `revision` and this digest.

Label.description: Participant-authored display text without control characters. Its UTF-8 encoding is at most 128 bytes (`x-pigloros-limits.label_bytes`, enforced at admission); `maxLength` is the coarse character bound that follows from it.

RevisionParent.description: The current head revision of the resource a new revision derives from.

Problem.description: A failure of the problem-types.json registry.

principal_denial_records_per_minute.source: apps/piglor-gateway MAX_DENIAL_RECORDS_PER_PRINCIPAL_PER_MINUTE (#1359); a fixed one-minute window that bounds durable denial evidence and never decides an authority result

denial_records_per_minute.source: apps/piglor-gateway MAX_DENIAL_RECORDS_PER_MINUTE (#1359); the host-wide bound of the same window

authority_denial_records.source: pos-core MAX_AUTHORIZATION_DENIAL_RECORDS (#1359); a full authority store refuses further denial evidence and never prunes it

identifier_length.source: pos-core MAX_AUTHORITY_TEXT_BYTES; ADR-064 owner IDs 1-128 bytes; identifiers are ASCII, so maxLength in characters is the byte bound

session_network_grants.source: chosen by #1362 (owner freeze decision): room for operator network grants beyond v1's two

label_bytes.source: pos-crypto plugin_manifest MAX_LABEL_BYTES; UTF-8 bytes checked at admission, Label maxLength is only the coarse character bound
